open_errors.issue: At the end of ch 2 Devan lifts the bar off its hooks and leans it against the wall beside the window. At dusk in ch 3 he lifts it 'from its hooks on the wall'.
open_errors.fix: Have him take the bar from where he leaned it.

patches.find: He lifted the long teak bar from its hooks on the wall and dropped it into the iron brackets, and the whole window shut like a mouth.
patches.replace: He lifted the long teak bar from where it leaned against the wall and dropped it into the iron brackets, and the whole window shut like a mouth.

open_errors.issue: In ch 8 the unlit lamp is the corridor lamp across from the chamber door, and Raiu is moved to the head of the stair. Neela's ch 16 reread places the unlit lamp 'at the stair head'.
open_errors.fix: Call it the corridor lamp outside the door.

patches.find: The lamp at the stair head, left unlit, so nothing would light her coming in at dawn half-dressed.
patches.replace: The corridor lamp outside the door, left unlit, so nothing would light her coming in at dawn half-dressed.

open_errors.issue: Ch 12 twice dates Asha's death to the rains ('since the rains she died'). Ch 17 says Ittan's letters began 'the winter Asha died'.

patches.find: He has written me a kind letter every season for six years. Since the winter Asha died.
patches.replace: He has written me a kind letter every season for six years. Since the rains Asha died.

open_errors.issue: In ch 16 Devan gives the shutters to Neela: 'The shutters are yours... I won't touch them.' From ch 17 on she opens and closes them herself. Ch 18 still calls them 'the shutters he closed every evening'.
open_errors.fix: Reflect that he no longer handles the shutters.

patches.find: and leaving behind the shutters he closed every evening and the sword he laid hilt-first on her side of the bed.
patches.replace: and leaving behind the shutters he no longer touched and the sword he laid hilt-first on her side of the bed.

open_errors.issue: The pass is sealed that same day, and the chapter later stresses that for four months nothing goes down, 'no rider'. Yet earlier in ch 29 Devan expects Muthu's letter to reach the palace 'before the week was out' and the council to hear 'within a month'.
open_errors.fix: Tie both expectations to the roads opening.

patches.find: whatever was said in this court would reach the palace in a grey-sealed letter before the week was out.
patches.replace: whatever was said in this court would go to the palace in a grey-sealed letter as soon as the road opened.

patches.find: The council would hear of it within a month.
patches.replace: The council would hear of it when the rains broke.

open_errors.issue: Neela recalls that when she asked why he barred the shutters he 'asked me about the terraces'. That never happens. In ch 3 he answers 'Rain' at dusk and repeats it the next dusk (ch 4). Devan also says she has carried the question 'since the third day', but the first barring is the second dusk (day 2).
open_errors.fix: Match the recalled exchange and the day to ch 3 and ch 4.

patches.find: When I asked why you bar the shutters, you asked me about the terraces. And the next dusk you said 'rain.'
patches.replace: When I asked why you bar the shutters, you said 'rain.' And the next dusk you said it again.

patches.find: You've been carrying one since the third day.
patches.replace: You've been carrying one since the second day.

open_errors.issue: Ch 29 states that once the pass is sealed no rider or writ can go down for four months. Muthu's packet is held in the strongbox 'for the spring rider'. Yet in ch 32 Devan says the closing writ with Neela's name is 'on her desk now', and Neela says the queen 'has my name already'. The queen cannot hold it until the roads open.
open_errors.fix: Make the queen's knowledge of the name a future event.

patches.find: She has your name. You signed the closing writ, 'of Kettamala'. It's on her desk now.
patches.replace: She'll have your name. You signed the closing writ, 'of Kettamala'. It goes to her desk with the first rider.

patches.find: She has my name already, Devan. Soon she'll have yours beside it.
patches.replace: She'll have my name with the first rider, Devan. Soon she'll have yours beside it.
